Rashi on Keritot 4a:10:1.hebrew: כל חלב כשב - דליכא השתא ג"ש:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:10:1.english: Any fat of a sheep - For now there is no verbal analogy [gezeirah shavah from Sinai].

Rashi on Keritot 4a:13:1.english: An ox has an increased [measure] of libations - [As it is written:] "Half a hin shall be for a bull" [Numbers 28:14].

Rashi on Keritot 4a:15:1.english: A goat has an increased [applicability] with regard to idol worship - In [the case of] an individual.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:16:1.hebrew: חד מתרי - הצד השוה שבהן, שהן מין בהמה וחלבו אסור, ואימורי בכוריהם קריבים:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:16:1.english: One from two - [By] the common denominator between them: that they are a species of domesticated animal and its fat is forbidden, and [so] the sacrificial portions of their firstborns are offered.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:17:1.english: They have increased [applicability] for idol worship - A bull for the community and a goat for an individual.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:18:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: מה לשור וכשב שכן יש בהן ריבוי אצל מזבח — שור בנסכים וכשב באליה, אבל עז אין בקרבנו ריבוי אצל מזבח:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:18:1.english: This is how we read [the text]: "What [is notable] about an ox and a sheep, in that they have an increased aspect at the altar" — an ox with [its] libations and a sheep with [its] fat-tail, whereas a goat has no increased aspect in its offering at the altar.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:1:1.hebrew: וישנו בלב - עיקר איסורו תלוי ברוע לבו, ידע למי גידף. הילכך, לא חשיב מעשה. אבל השתחואה, אנו רואין משתחוה לעבודת כוכבים:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:1:1.english: And it is in the heart - The essence of its prohibition depends on the evil of his heart, [that] he knew whom he blasphemed. Therefore, it is not considered an action. However, [in the case of] bowing down, we see [him] bowing down to idolatry.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:1:2.hebrew: גליון: הואיל וישנו בלב - עיקר איסורו במחשבת הלב, ואין כאן מעשה, ומה שמדבר אינו אלא משמיע איסורו; אבל כפיפת קומתו היינו עיקר איסורו, דאילו היה מדבר במקבל עבודת כוכבים בלא השתחואה, לא מחייב, דאין עיקר בלב אלא כפיפה היא החיוב. נראה לי:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:1:2.english: Marginal gloss: Since it is in the heart - The essence of its prohibition is in the thought of the heart, and there is no action here, and what he speaks is merely making his prohibition heard. However, bowing one's stature [in idol worship] is the essence of its prohibition; for if one were to speak [as] one who accepts idolatry without bowing, he would not be liable, since the essence is not in the heart, rather the bowing is [what causes] the liability. So it appears to me.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:20:1.hebrew: הא כי כתיב קרא בעניינא דקדשים כתיב - דכתיב (ויקרא ז) כי כל אוכל חלב מן הבהמה וגו', והואיל ובעניינא דקדשים כתיב, ודאי אין חיה נוהגת בהו. הלכך, לא איצטריך שור וכבש למישרי חיה:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:20:1.english: When the verse is written, it is written in the context of sacrifices - As it is written (Leviticus 7[:25]): "For whoever eats the fat of the animal, etc." And since it is written in the context of sacrifices, certainly [the prohibition of forbidden fat] does not apply to an undomesticated animal. Therefore, [the mention of] "ox and sheep" is not needed to permit [the fat of] an undomesticated animal.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:21:1.hebrew: מכלל דרבנן סברי - לא ילפינן לאו דכל חלב מעניינו, בתמיה:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:21:1.english: By inference, the Rabbis maintain - [that] we do not derive the prohibition of "any fat" from its context? [This is asked] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:21:2.hebrew: דכולי עלמא ילפינן דבר למד מעניינו - בעלמא, אבל הכא לאו עניינו, דהאי לאו והאי כרת:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:21:2.english: Everyone [agrees] we derive a matter learned from its context - In general; but here it is not [considered] its context, since this [one] is a [regular] prohibition and that [one] is karet.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:21:3.hebrew: והכא בהא קמיפלגי כו' - גירסא זו הכתובה בספרים משובשת היא, ועל ידי פרשנים טועין שלא היו בקיאין בשמועה, ופירשוה בשיבוש בתוך הגירסא. וכך הצעה ולא יותר: "והכא בהא קמיפלגי, מר סבר למידין לאו מלאו ולאו מכרת, ומר סבר לאו מלאו ילפינן, לאו מכרת לא ילפינן". והכי פירושא: ר' ישמעאל סבר למידין דבר מעניינו, בין לאו מלאו, בין לאו מכרת:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:21:3.english: And here it is about this that they disagree, etc. - This reading that is written in the books is corrupt, and [it came about] through erring commentators who were not well-versed in the teaching, and they explained it erroneously [by inserting their words] into the text. And thus is the text, and nothing more: "And here it is about this that they disagree: One Sage holds [that] we derive a prohibition from a prohibition and a prohibition from [a prohibition punishable by] karet, and one Sage holds [that] we derive a prohibition from a prohibition, [but] we do not derive a prohibition from [a prohibition punishable by] karet." And this is its explanation: Rabbi Yishmael holds [that] we derive a matter from its context, whether [it is] a prohibition from a prohibition, [or] whether [it is] a prohibition from [a prohibition punishable by] karet.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:24:1.hebrew: ורבנן סברי - לאו מלאו למידין זה מזה כשהן בפרשה אחת, דבר למד מעניינו, כי ההיא דבשר בחלב השנויה בפ' כל הבשר (חולין קטו:), "לא תאכלנו" — בבשר בחלב הכתוב מדבר. אבל לאו מכרת, כעין הכא, לא ילפינן דבר למד מעניינו; הלכך, אי לא כתיב "שור וכשב ועז", ה"א חיה במשמע:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:24:1.english: And the Rabbis hold - [Regarding] a prohibition from a prohibition, we derive one from the other when they are in one section [through the principle of] a matter learned from its context — like that [teaching] of meat with milk that is taught in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaBasar (Chullin 115b): "You shall not eat it" — Scripture is speaking of meat with milk. However, [regarding] a prohibition from [a prohibition punishable by] karet, such as here, we do not derive [it through] a matter learned from its context. Therefore, if "ox, and sheep, and goat" were not written, I would have said [that] an undomesticated animal is included.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:25:1.english: And if you wish, say [this is] the reason of the Rabbis - Because this [verse,] "ox, and sheep, and goat," is needed by them for [the statement] of Rav Mari.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:25:2.english: The tail of a non-sacred [animal] should be prohibited - For it is called fat, in the chapter [entitled] Kol HaBasar (Chullin 117a).

Rashi on Keritot 4a:25:3.hebrew: ששוה בשלשתן - שנקרא חלב בשלשתן, ואליה לא איקרי חלב אלא בכשב:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:25:3.english: That is equal in [all] three of them - That it is called fat [chelev] in [all] three of them, whereas the tail is only called fat in [the case of] a sheep.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:26:1.hebrew: א"כ נכתוב כל חלב שור וכשב - ומהתם ממעיטנא אליה, דבעינן דבר השוה בשניהן:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:26:1.english: If so, let [the verse] write: "any fat of ox and sheep" - And from there I would exclude the fat tail, since we require something that is equal in both of them.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:27:1.hebrew: לאו דעריות - להכי נקט עריות, דאיכא מילי טובא ואיכא לאו בכל חדא:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:27:1.english: The prohibition of forbidden sexual relations - This is why he mentioned forbidden sexual relations: because there are many [distinct] cases, and there is a prohibition for each one.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:28:1.hebrew: מאחת מהנה - משמע מאחת חייב, הנה כמה חטאות:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:28:1.english: From one of them - This implies: for one [transgression] he is liable, [and] "them" [implies] several sin-offerings.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:29:1.english: [Forbidden] fat and [forbidden] fat - Two olive-bulks of [forbidden] fat.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:29:2.hebrew: שם אחד - חלב הכליות או חלב הדקין. שם אחד בהעלם אחד ל"ג:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:29:2.english: One category - [Such as] fat of the kidneys or fat of the intestines. We do not read [in the text]: "one category in one lapse of awareness."

Rashi on Keritot 4a:29:3.hebrew: שני שמות - כזית משעל הכוליא, וכזית משעל הדקין:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:29:3.english: Two categories - An olive-bulk from [the fat] upon the kidney, and an olive-bulk from [the fat] upon the intestines.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:2:1.hebrew: יצאו עדים זוממין - בתורת כהנים גבי פר כהן משיח, והכי אמרינן: אחר שריבינו דברים שהן בעבודת כוכבים ודברים שאינן בעבודת כוכבים, יכול שאני מרבה המסית והמדיח ועדים זוממין? ת"ל "ועשה" — יצאו אלו שאין בהן מעשה; יצאו מכלל חטאת:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:2:1.english: Except for conspiring witnesses - [This is taught] in Torat Kohanim regarding the bull of the anointed priest, and thus we say [there]: After we have included matters that involve idolatry and matters that do not involve idolatry, might [I think] that I include one who incites [to idolatry], one who leads [others] astray, and conspiring witnesses? The verse states: "and he does" — excluded are these, which do not involve an action; [that is,] they are excluded from the category of a sin offering.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:2:2.english: And is it not written with regard to them, “at the mouth” - And let us say [that] the twisting of his mouth is [considered] an action.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:2:3.hebrew: הואיל וישנן בראייה - עיקר עדותן בראיית העין, שמעידין מה שראו; הילכך לא חשיב מעשה:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:2:3.english: Since they are [dependent] on sight - The essence of their testimony is through the sight of the eye, as they testify [to] what they saw; therefore, it is not considered an action.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:30:1.hebrew: דהעלמות מחלקין - דכיון דנודע לו בינתים, הרי הן שתי שגגות, וחטאת בידיעה תלה רחמנא, דכתיב (ויקרא ד) או הודע אליו:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:30:1.english: That the lapses of awareness separate - For since it became known to him in between, they are [considered] two unwitting transgressions, and the Merciful One made [liability for] a sin offering dependent upon knowledge, as it is written (Leviticus 4): "Or [if his sin] be made known to him."

Rashi on Keritot 4a:31:1.hebrew: חלב דנותר - דאיכא שתי שגגות משתי כריתות — חלב ונותר — וחייב שתי חטאות:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:31:1.english: Forbidden fat of notar - For there are two unwitting transgressions of two [prohibitions punishable by] karet — forbidden fat and notar — and he is liable [to bring] two sin offerings.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:31:2.english: Let him be liable due to [eating] sacrificial [food] as well - [to bring] a guilt offering for misuse of consecrated property.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:32:1.hebrew: אלא אמר רב ששת כגון שאכל חלב דקודש - ולעולם משום חלב חייב שתים, ולהכי לא חשיב אשם מעילות, אלא של שם אחד. ורבי יהודה היא, דמחייב אחלב מוקדשין שתים משום חלב; ושני שמות דקתני, משום דבחלב מוקדשין כתיבי תרי קראי:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:32:1.english: Rather, Rav Sheshet said: [Here we are dealing with] a case where he ate forbidden fat of sacrificial [food] - And in fact, it is on account of forbidden fat [that] he is liable [to bring] two [sin offerings], and that is why [the baraita] does not count a guilt offering for misuse of consecrated property, [reckoning] only [the sin offerings] of one category. And [this] is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yehuda, who renders one liable for forbidden fat of sacrificial animals [to] two [offerings] on account of forbidden fat; and [the phrase] "two categories" that [the baraita] teaches is because two verses are written regarding forbidden fat of sacrificial animals.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:32:2.hebrew: חלב נבלה לוקה שתים - משום חלב ומשום נבלה, והמוקדשין משום חלב ומשום זרות:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:32:2.english: [One who eats] forbidden fat of an animal carcass is flogged [with] two [sets of lashes] - Because of [the prohibition of] forbidden fat and because of [the prohibition of] an animal carcass; and [for] sacrificial [animals], because of [the prohibition of] forbidden fat and because of [the prohibition against] a non-priest [partaking of them]:

Rashi on Keritot 4a:32:3.hebrew: ג' - ב' משום חלב, כדמפ' לקמן, וא' משום זרות:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:32:3.english: Three [sets of lashes] - Two on account of [eating] forbidden fat, as [the Gemara] explains below, and one on account of [the prohibition against] a non-priest [eating sacrificial food].

Rashi on Keritot 4a:33:1.hebrew: ונוקמה - להא דלעיל דקתני ב' שמות, כלומר משתי בהמות משני מינין, ור' ישמעאל היא:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:33:1.english: And let us interpret it - [referring to] this [teaching] above that teaches "two names [categories]," that is to say, [forbidden fat] from two animals of two [different] species, and it is [in accordance with] Rabbi Yishmael.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:3:1.english: Liable for each and every one - [for] lashes, if he ate them with a single warning.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:4:1.english: One is flogged for [violating] a general prohibition - For each and every one.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:4:2.hebrew: ורבנן סברי אין לוקין - ואי תיקשי: לא לילקי אפילו חדא? דחדא מיהא לקי:
Rashi on Keritot 4a:4:2.english: And the Rabbis maintain one is not flogged - And if you ask: He should not be flogged even once? [No,] for he is at least flogged once.

Rashi on Keritot 4a:8:1.hebrew: ויליף שור שור משבת - למען ינוח שורך (שמות כ״ג:י״ב), מה התם חיה ועוף כיוצא בו, דהכי מוקמינן בב"ק בפרק שור שנגח את הפרה (בבא קמא דף נד: ע"ש):
Rashi on Keritot 4a:8:1.english: And it derives "ox" [from] "ox" from Shabbat - [As it is written:] "That your ox may rest" (Exodus 23:12): just as there, undomesticated animals and birds are [included] like it, as we establish thus in Bava Kamma in the chapter [entitled] Shor SheNagach Et HaParah (Bava Kamma 54b; see there).
